transcript.content: Hello, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because of what’s been going on with my husband’s sister. She’s been working things in the family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. People keep trying to smooth it over like it’s nothing, but I know what I’ve been seeing. This has been going on for more than a year now.
Aside from your concerns about your sister-in-law, have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people don't seem to notice?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t hear voices or see things like that. This is more about what people are doing and the way things are being handled.
Aside from this situation with your sister-in-law, would you say you generally have a hard time trusting people in other areas of your life, or is this distrust specific to her and this situation?

It’s mostly specific to her and what’s going on there. I still go to my quilting group, choir practice, my GED lessons, and the senior walks like I always have. I’m not walking around distrusting everybody. It’s just changed how I deal with my husband’s sister, and some family gatherings I don’t feel comfortable going to now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre belief that her sister-in-law is manipulating the family business to seize control and marginalize her, persisting for over a year. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, and no broader impairment in functioning—she continues to engage in her usual social activities (quilting, choir, GED classes, senior walks) and her mistrust is circumscribed to the specific individual/situation rather than pervasive. This pattern—an isolated, non-bizarre delusion without other psychotic symptoms, preserved functioning outside the delusional theme, and duration >1 month—is characteristic of Delusional Disorder (F22) rather than Schizophrenia (which requires broader psychotic symptoms and functional decline) or Paranoid Personality Disorder (which would involve pervasive distrust across contexts, not an isolated delusional belief).
